acceptance: The intended validation status for a seeded DataFrame TPC-H run with skipped parameter-sensitive counts is decided and recorded
SQL and DataFrame paths either agree or the difference is documented where maintainers stage bundles
context:
2026-11-12: owner decision: do not start this until PR 4154 (fix/correctness-gates, another session) merges; it rewrites the same row-count validation files (benchbox/core/validation/query_validation.py, benchbox/core/dataframe/query_validation.py, benchbox/core/results/query_execution.py). Re-diagnose on develop after it lands.

2026-11-15 re-diagnosis on develop 21b0b2beb7 (after PR 4154). Five whys: (1) A seeded TPC-H bundle cannot be published: the DataFrame bundle says `uncertain` and staging skips it; the SQL bundle says `passed` but validate_submission.py rejects it with `summary.validation='passed' contradicts queries[i].row_count_validation.status='SKIPPED'` (20 such errors on a seeded DuckDB SF 1 bundle made today). (2) The rows are SKIPPED because the only reference row counts are for qgen default parameters and a seed changes the parameters. (3) The SQL summary still says passed because ResultBuilder.build and the runner start at PASSED and lower it only for a failure or an UNVALIDATED row; they never look at SKIPPED. The DataFrame summary (PR 1886) and the bundle validator (_validate_execution_consistency) each carry their own rule, and those two agree: passed means every row count was checked. (4) The three rules never met: 431 of 435 `passed` bundles in results-data carry no row_count_validation at all, so the validator rule had only ever seen DataFrame evidence until SQL rows began carrying it. (5) Nothing ties what a producer may summarise as passed to what the validator accepts; each side is tested alone. Root cause: the run-level meaning of passed is defined three times and not enforced at production time. Owner first chose to loosen the DataFrame rule; that produced a bundle that stages and then fails validation, so it was dropped. Owner then asked for the root cause to be corrected: the SQL builder and runner now record UNCERTAIN when a row count was SKIPPED or ERROR, with a test that runs a built payload through the validator check.

2026-11-16 correction: PR 4260 merged while the change above was in review and settled the rule the other way: a passed run may carry SKIPPED row counts that have a documented reason (data refreshed, within tolerance, within range), and the validator accepts them. PR 4266 (any skip gives uncertain) was closed unmerged. Replacement PR 4269 builds on the merged rule: 'parameter sensitive' becomes a documented skip reason and the DataFrame summary treats documented skips as neutral once at least one row count was checked. Verified with --seed 42 TPC-H SF 0.01 on DuckDB and Polars DataFrame: both passed, staged, and validate_submission.py reported 0 errors. A seeded DataFrame TPC-H run at SF 1 still has no reference and stays uncertain (documented in docs/agent/maintainer-bundles.md).

PR 4269 merged to develop as 4c848ffdd6 on 2026-11-16.
description: Found 2026-11-11. With `--seed 42` at SF 0.01, DuckDB (SQL) and Polars DataFrame both skip the 8 parameter-sensitive row counts (Q2, Q9, Q11, Q13, Q16, Q18, Q20, Q21). The SQL bundle records summary.validation `passed`; the DataFrame bundle records `uncertain` (benchbox/core/dataframe/query_validation.py: any skipped row gives UNCERTAIN), so corpus staging skips it as validation_not_clean. At SF 1 a seeded DataFrame run has no reference at all, and `--official` requires a seed, so no DataFrame TPC-H bundle can be both official and stageable. The live corpus shows the effect: every Polars TPC-H result is unranked. Without a seed the Polars SF 0.1 run validates 22 of 22 and stages. Decide whether the stricter DataFrame rule is intended; if so document that DataFrame corpus runs must use default parameters, and if not align the two paths.
